setting_and_object.category: Architecture + training-objective co-design (empirical existence proof of sample-efficient pretraining)

details: LLM pretraining on internet-scale raw text spends most compute predicting task-irrelevant/prompt tokens, making from-scratch foundational research inaccessible outside compute-rich labs.
Scaling recurrent (multi-timescale) architectures to language is blocked by gradient instability from deep recurrence.

HRM-Text: a from-scratch language model replacing the Transformer stack with a dual-timescale Hierarchical Recurrent Model (slow H module updated once per cycle, fast L module iterated inside each cycle), stabilized by MagicNorm (internal PreNorm blocks inside each recurrent module plus a final norm on the recurrent pathway, exploiting the forward-N vs truncated-backward-K asymmetry) and warmup deep credit assignment (backward horizon K grown from 2 to 5 recurrent steps).

Co-designed objective: skip raw-text pretraining entirely and pretrain from random initialization on instruction-response pairs with a response-only task-completion loss -log P(x_a | x_q) plus a PrefixLM mask (bidirectional over instruction, causal over response).

Open-source task-formatted mixture (general instructions, rewritten knowledge, math/symbolic tasks, textbook exercises, web-extracted questions): ~176.5B tokens / 593.7M docs corpus, sampled to 40B unique tokens, 60B total training tokens.
SeqIO-style stratified sampling with per-task/dataset document caps and upsampling of small sets; condition tags prepended (direct, cot, synth, noisy) for conditioned generation.
All <think>...</think> long-CoT traces stripped so the model relies on internal recurrent computation.
BPE tokenizer, 65,536 vocab; 4,096 context.
HRM-Text 1B: each of H and L modules is a 16-layer transformer, hidden 1536, head dim 128; parameterless RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE (theta=1e4), sigmoid-gated attention.
Recurrence schedule H2L3: 2 outer H cycles each with 3 L steps (8 module steps ~ 4 recursions); logits from final H state.
Adam-atan2 (beta 0.9/0.95, wd 0.1), constant LR 2.2e-4 after 2k-step warmup, no grad clipping, batch 196,608 tokens, bfloat16, EMA (0.9999) checkpoint used for eval.
46 hours on 2x8 H100 (FSDP2), ~$1,472; single continuous run without checkpoint recovery or loss-spike skipping.
FLOPs-matched architecture comparison: standard Transformer, larger matched-FLOPs Transformer, Looped/Universal Transformer, RINS, TRM (parameter-shared HRM variant), HRM.
Open model comparison: Llama, Qwen, Gemma, OLMo, and recurrent-depth models Huginn and Ouro (2-7B, up to 36T tokens).
Benchmarks include MMLU, ARC-C, DROP, GSM8K, MATH; temperature 0, no system prompt, 3072-token eval context; few-shot via vLLM, CoT via lm_eval_harness.
FLOPs accounting: 6ND for dense models; 2ND forward + 4ND backward scaled by recurrent steps per pass.
Incremental FLOPs-matched ablation: Transformer + causal full-sequence loss -> + task-completion (response-only) loss -> + PrefixLM -> + HRM architecture.
Effective-depth probes: adjacent-block representation difference norms, block-wise cosine similarity, and logit-lens KL to final distribution.

Gradient-stability diagnostics: mean absolute gradient magnitude, log-magnitude dispersion Std(log|g|), Jacobian growth, tail-to-median ratio, varying backward H/L cycles and comparing HRM vs RINS vs Universal Transformer.

Contamination test adapted from Llama (13- and 20-gram overlap, Clean/Not-Clean/Not-Dirty/Dirty subsets, |Z|>2 criterion); inference-time auto-guidance interpolating/extrapolating logits across H loops (w in {-0.5,...,0.5}).

key_findings.finding: A 1B recurrent model pretrained from scratch on only 40B unique tokens reaches the performance range of 2-7B open models at drastically lower cost.
key_findings.evidence: HRM-Text 1B scores 60.7% MMLU, 81.9% ARC-C, 82.2% DROP, 84.5% GSM8K, 56.2% MATH from a single checkpoint, using roughly 100-900x fewer training tokens and 96-432x less estimated training compute than Llama/Qwen/Gemma/OLMo/Huginn/Ouro baselines, trained in 46 hours on 16 H100s for ~$1,472.

key_findings.finding: Both the response-only task-completion objective and PrefixLM masking independently raise per-example yield, and the HRM architecture adds a further gain on top.
key_findings.evidence: A FLOPs-matched incremental ablation (Transformer + causal full-sequence loss -> + task-completion loss -> + PrefixLM -> HRM) shows consistent improvements at each step across benchmarks; total loss is comparable with/without the task-completion objective while response-token loss is substantially lower, and PrefixLM yields higher attention softmax entropy and more global (less localized) attention.

key_findings.finding: Under matched training FLOPs, hierarchical dual-timescale recurrence is the strongest point in the recurrent-architecture design space.
key_findings.evidence: Looped Transformers and RINS beat same-size Transformers but are inconsistent against a larger FLOPs-matched Transformer, whereas HRM performs well against all listed baselines including the larger deep Transformer; HRM also matches or beats TRM (H/L parameter sharing) while using substantially fewer FLOPs, with TRM unstable when recursions are reduced to match parameters.

key_findings.finding: HRM's advantage is attributable to greater effective depth rather than parameter count.
key_findings.evidence: Adjacent-block difference norms and block-wise cosine similarity show more active representational change across depth for HRM, and logit-lens KL to the final distribution stays large in deep layers for HRM while standard and looped Transformers stabilize their output distribution early.

key_findings.finding: Instability from deep recurrent backpropagation stems from rare multiplicative gradient spikes, which truncation plus warmup and MagicNorm control.
key_findings.evidence: Increasing the backward horizon toward full BPTT produces intermittent high-amplitude gradient events, higher log-magnitude dispersion Std(log|g|) (driven mainly by H-cycle depth), and larger Jacobian growth; paired full-vs-truncated checkpoints show full BPTT is usually comparable but occasionally far larger, and HRM's chosen truncation matches Universal Transformer stability (higher median gradient, lower tail-to-median) while outperforming RINS.
